post.summary: Stream a simulation for the session Petri net
post.description:
Stream a discrete-event simulation for the session's Petri net.

Returns ``text/event-stream`` chunks terminated by ``data: [DONE]``.

**Two snapshot modes**

* **Time-based** (default): one snapshot every ``time_step`` simulation units.
* **Step-based** (scientific): one snapshot every ``snapshot_interval`` transition firings.

Parse a PNML document into net_data, without touching any session
post.description:
Parse *xml* (PNML, from PetriObjModelPaint or from this
application's own export) into the frontend-shape net_data dict this
application already reads and writes everywhere else, plus every
non-fatal warning parse_pnml encountered along the way.

Raises 400 for the two structural failures the reader cannot soft-fix
around: a document with no <pnml> root, or a <pnml> with no <net>.
Everything else it cannot make full sense of is downgraded to a
warning in the response instead of failing the whole request.

post.summary: Stream a simulation for an arbitrary Petri net
post.description:
Stream a discrete-event simulation for the provided Petri net.

Unlike the session-scoped endpoint, this does not require or create a
session.  The caller supplies the full net JSON in the request body.

Returns ``text/event-stream`` chunks of shape
``{current_time, step_number, markings, buffers, progress, fired_transitions,
firing_sequence}`` terminated by ``data: [DONE]``.  ``firing_sequence`` is
the ordered list of atomic highlight steps since the previous frame; it is
empty when nothing fired, or when a remote backend does not report phases.

post.summary: Stream a simulation for a composed Petri-object model (v2)
post.description:
Stream a discrete-event simulation for a composed Petri-object model.

Mirrors the flat-net endpoint's remote/local split: with no
``SIMULATION_REMOTE_URL`` configured, or when it's unreachable and
``SIMULATION_REMOTE_FALLBACK`` is set, this runs on the built-in local
engine (``build_composed_sim_net`` + ``PetriSimulator``) instead of
petri-server. The one gap is placeToTransition links, which the local
engine does not support (see ``ComposedSimulationUnsupported``) — a model
using one always needs the remote engine.

post.summary: Export + parse a composed model, no simulation run
post.description:
Cheap way to verify a composed model (including its links) before
spending a full simulation run on it.

With ``SIMULATION_REMOTE_URL`` configured, round-trips the generated
PNML through petri-server's real ``POST /api/v2/model/parse``. With no
remote configured, validates locally instead (see `_local_preview`):
the exact same PNML this route would otherwise have sent to
petri-server is round-tripped through this application's own importer.
Either way the response states which validator ran (petri-server's own
response shape for the remote path; a ``"validator": "local"`` field
for the fallback).

post.summary: Chat Completions
post.description:
OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoint.

Supports both streaming (stream=true) and non-streaming modes.

Credentials are resolved before any agent invocation (BYOK-only):
  - ``metadata.llm_credential_id`` → BYOK using the user's profile.
  - missing → 402 byok_required.

Authorization is performed via a signed ?token query parameter so that
download links can be opened directly in a browser (where the Authorization
header is not available). The token is single-purpose (type=download),
short-lived, and bound to the specific file_id and user_id.

AgentEventDelta.title: AgentEventDelta
AgentEventDelta.description:
Non-standard streaming extension: agent reasoning step.

Emitted as `delta.agent_event` on chunk choices so OpenAI-compatible
clients that don't know about it simply ignore the field. The
Petri Net Sim UI renders each event as a step card inside the assistant
message. Tool-call events ride on AIMessage tool_calls (Anthropic
tool_use blocks parsed by LangChain); tool_result events ride on
ToolMessage outputs from the LangGraph tool node.

SimulateBody.title: SimulateBody
SimulateBody.description:
Optional body for the simulate endpoint.

Resolution order:
1. ``snapshot_id``  — fetch the specific versioned snapshot from DB (preferred).
2. ``net_data``     — legacy fallback: full net JSON from the frontend
                      (used by old messages in localStorage that pre-date snapshots).
3. Neither          — use the session's current ``net_data`` from the sessions table.
